cues.en: Math is sometimes a real tease. It seduces us with the beauty of reasoning geometrically in two and three dimensions where there's this really nice back and forth between pairs or triplets of numbers and spatial stuff that our visual cortex is good at processing. For example, if you think about a circle with radius 1 centered at the origin, you are in effect conceptualizing every possible pair of numbers, x and y,
cues.zh: 数学有时真的很吊人胃口。它用二维和三维中几何推理的美感诱惑着我们，在二元组或三元组与我们视觉皮层擅长处理的空间事物之间，存在着这种非常美妙的来回呼应。比如，想象一个以原点为中心、半径为 1 的圆，你实际上是在对所有可能的数对 x 和 y 进行概念化，

cues.en: that satisfy a certain numerical property that x squared plus y squared is 1. And the usefulness here is that a lot of facts that look opaque in a purely analytic context become quite clear geometrically and vice versa. Honestly, this channel has been the direct beneficiary of this back and forth since it offers such a rich library of that special category of cleverness that involves connecting two seemingly disparate ideas.
cues.zh: 这些数对满足某个数值特性，即 x 的平方加 y 的平方等于 1。这种方法的用处在于，许多在纯分析语境下显得晦涩的事实，从几何角度来看会变得十分清晰，反之亦然。说实话，本频道一直直接受益于这种呼应，因为它提供了一座宝库，专门存放那种将两个看似毫不相干的想法联系起来的绝妙巧思。

cues.en: And I don't just mean the general back and forth between pairs or triplets of numbers and spatial reasoning. I mean this specific one between sums of squares and circles and spheres. It's at the heart of the video I made showing how pi is connected to number theory and primes, and the one showing how to visualize all possible Pythagorean triples. It also underlies the video on the Borsuk-Ulam theorem being used to solve what was basically a counting puzzle by using topological facts about spheres.
cues.zh: 我指的不仅是数对、三元组与空间推理之间普遍的来回呼应，我说的正是平方和与圆以及球体之间这种具体的呼应。它是我之前视频的核心：一个展示了圆周率如何与数论和质数联系起来，另一个展示了如何可视化所有可能的勾股数。它也是那个用 Borsuk-Ulam 定理解题的视频的基础，当时我们利用球体的拓扑学事实，解决了一个本质上是计数的谜题。

cues.en: There is no doubt that the ability to frame analytic facts geometrically is very useful for math. But it's all a tease, because when you start asking questions about quadruplets, or quintuplets, or 100 tuples of numbers, it's frustrating. The constraints on our physical space seem to have constrained our intuitions about geometry, and we lose this back and forth.
cues.zh: 毫无疑问，将分析事实用几何形式表达出来的能力，在数学中是非常有用的。但这全都是吊人胃口，因为当你开始探讨四元组、五元组，乃至 100 元数组的问题时，就会感到非常沮丧。我们物理空间的局限似乎限制了我们的几何直觉，而我们也失去了这种来回呼应的能力。

cues.en: I mean, it is completely reasonable to imagine that there are problems out there that would have clever and illuminating solutions if only we knew how to conceptualize, say, lists of ten numbers as individual points in some space. For mathematicians, or computer scientists, or physicists, problems that are framed in terms of lists of numbers, lists of more than three numbers, are a regular part of the job.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，完全有理由相信，世上存在着许多问题，只要我们懂得如何将比如包含十个数字的列表概念化为某个空间中的单个点，就能得到巧妙且富有启发性的解答。对于数学家、计算机科学家或物理学家来说，用数字列表——包含三个以上数字的列表——来表述问题，完全是家常便饭。

cues.en: And the standard approach to actually doing math in higher dimensions is to use two and three dimensions for analogy, but to fundamentally reason about things just analytically, somewhat analogous to a pilot relying primarily on instruments and not sight while flying through the clouds. Now what I want to offer here is a hybrid between the purely geometric and the purely analytic views, a method for making the analytic reasoning a little more visual in a way that generalizes to arbitrarily high dimensions.
cues.zh: 而真正进行高维数学研究的标准方法，是利用二维和三维来进行类比，但从根本上只通过纯分析的方式来推导，这有点像飞行员在穿云飞行时，主要依赖仪表而不是肉眼。而我在这里想要提供的，是介于纯几何与纯分析视角之间的一种混合方法，一种让分析推理变得更具视觉感的方式，而且它可以推广到任意高维度。

cues.en: And to drive home the value of a tactic like this, I want to share with you a very famous example where analogies with two and three dimensions cannot help because of something extremely counterintuitive that only happens in higher dimensions. The hope, though, is that what I show you here helps to make that phenomenon more intuitive. The focus throughout will be on higher dimensional spheres. For example, when we talk about a four-dimensional sphere, say with radius 1 centered at the origin,
cues.zh: 为了说明这类策略的价值，我想分享一个非常著名的例子：在这个例子里，用二维和三维的类比帮不上忙，因为有些极其反直觉的现象只会在更高维发生。不过，我希望我在这里展示的内容能帮助你把那个现象变得更直观。整段内容的重点都会放在高维球面上。比如，当我们谈一个四维球面，比如说半径为 1、球心在原点，

cues.en: What that actually is, is the set of all quadruplets of numbers, x, y, z, w, where the sum of the squares of these numbers is 1. What I have pictured here now is multiple three-dimensional slices of a 4D sphere projected back into three dimensions. But it's confusing, and even if you do wrap your head around it, it just pushes the question back to how you would think about a 5, or a 6, or a 7-dimensional sphere. And more importantly,
cues.zh: 它实际上就是所有四元组 x、y、z、w 的集合，其中这些数的平方和为 1。现在图里展示的是一个四维球面的多个三维切片，再投影回三维。但这很让人困惑，而且就算你勉强想明白了，问题也只是被推回到：那五维、六维、七维球面该怎么想？更重要的是，

cues.en: Squinting your eyes to understand a projection like this is not very reflective of what doing math with a 4D sphere actually entails. Instead, the basic idea here will be to get very literal about it and to think about four separate numbers. I like to picture four vertical number lines with sliders to represent each number. Each configuration of these sliders is a point in 4D space, a quadruplet of numbers.
cues.zh: 眯着眼去理解这样的投影，并不能很好地反映用四维球面做数学到底是怎么回事。相反，这里的基本思路是：非常字面地看待它，去想四个独立的数。我喜欢把四条竖直的数轴画出来，每条上的滑块代表一个数。这些滑块的每一种位置组合，都是四维空间中的一个点，也就是一个四元组。

cues.en: And what it means to be on a 4D unit sphere, centered at the origin, is that the sum of the squares of these four values is 1. Our goal is to understand which movements of these sliders correspond to movements on the sphere. To do that, it helps if we knock things down to two dimensions where we can actually see the circle. So ask yourself, what's a nice way to think about this relation, that x squared plus y squared is 1?
cues.zh: 而位于以原点为球心的四维单位球面上，意思是这四个值的平方和为 1。我们的目标是理解滑块的哪些移动对应球面上的移动。要做到这一点，先把问题降到二维会有帮助，因为在二维我们真的能看见那个圆。所以问问自己：对于 x² + y² = 1 这个关系，怎样想比较自然？

cues.en: Well, I like to think of the value of x squared as the real estate belonging to x and likewise the value of y squared is the real estate belonging to y and that they have a total of one unit of real estate to share between them. So moving around on the circle corresponds to a constant exchange of real estate between the two variables. Part of the reason I choose this term is that it lets us make a very useful analogy that real estate is cheap near zero
cues.zh: 我喜欢把 x² 的值想成属于 x 的地产，同样，y² 的值是属于 y 的地产，而它们总共只有一单位地产可以分配。所以，在圆上移动，就对应两个变量之间不断地交换地产。我选择这个说法，部分原因是它能给出一个很有用的类比：地产在 0 附近很便宜，

cues.en: and more expensive away from 0. To see this, consider starting off in a position where x equals 1 and y is 0, meaning x has all of the real estate to itself, which in our usual geometric picture means we're on the rightmost point of the circle. If you move x down just a bit to 0.9, the value of x squared changes to 0.81, so it has in effect given up 0.19 units of real estate.
cues.zh: 离 0 越远就越贵。为了看清这一点，设想从 x 等于 1、y 等于 0 的位置出发，这意味着 x 独占全部地产，在我们平常的几何图景里，就是位于圆的最右端。如果你把 x 稍稍降到 0.9，x² 的值就变成 0.81，所以它实际上让出了 0.19 单位地产。

cues.en: But for y squared to increase by that same amount, y has to move an entire 0.44 units away from 0, more than 4 times the amount that x moved. In other words, x changed a little to give up expensive real estate, so that y could move a lot and gain the same value of cheap real estate. In terms of the usual circle drawing, this corresponds to the steep slope near the right side. A small nudge in x allows for a very big change to y.
cues.zh: 但如果 y 的平方要增加相同的量，y 必须远离 0 整整 0.44 个单位，是 x 移动距离的 4 倍还多。换句话说，x 只变化了一点点，就让出了“昂贵的地皮”，从而让 y 能够移动很大一段距离，获得等值的“廉价地皮”。在平时的圆形图示中，这就对应了右侧附近的陡峭斜率。x 稍微动一点，就能引起 y 的巨大改变。

cues.en: Moving forward, let's add some tick marks to these lines to indicate what 0.05 units of real estate looks like at each point. That is, how much would X have to change so that the value of X squared changes by 0.05? As you walk around the circle, the trade-off in value between X squared and Y squared gives this piston-looking dance motion where the sliders are moving more slowly away from zero because real estate is more expensive in those regions.
cues.zh: 接下来，我们在这些线上加一些刻度线，用来表示在每个点上 0.05 个单位的“地皮”是什么样的。也就是说，x 需要改变多少，才能让 x 的平方变化 0.05？当你绕着圆走时，x 平方和 y 平方之间的价值置换，会呈现出一种类似活塞的舞蹈运动，滑块在远离零点时移动得更慢，因为那些区域的“地皮”更昂贵。

cues.en: there are just more tick marks to cover per unit distance. Also a nice side effect of the term real estate is that it aligns naturally with the fact that it comes in units of distance squared. So the square root of the total real estate among all coordinates gives us the distance from the origin. For a unit sphere in three dimensions, the set of all triplets x, y, z where the sum of their squares is one, all we have to do is add a third slider for z.
cues.zh: 在单位距离内需要经过的刻度线也更多。而且用“地皮”这个词还有一个好处，它天然契合了以距离平方为单位这一事实。因此，所有坐标占据的总地皮的平方根，就给出了到原点的距离。对于三维空间中的单位球面——也就是所有平方和为 1 的三元组 x, y, z 的集合——我们只需要为 z 添加第三个滑块。

cues.en: But these three sliders still only have the one unit of real estate to share between them. To get a feel for this, imagine holding X in place at 0.5, where it occupies 0.25 units of real estate. What this means is that Y and Z can move around in the same piston-dense motion we saw before as they trade off the remaining 0.75 units of real estate. In terms of our typical way of visualizing a sphere,
cues.zh: 但即便有三个滑块，它们能共享的地皮依然只有 1 个单位。为了直观感受这一点，想象一下把 x 固定在 0.5 的位置，此时它占据了 0.25 个单位的地皮。这意味着 y 和 z 可以在剩下的 0.75 个单位地皮中进行权衡置换，呈现出我们之前见过的活塞式运动。以我们平时可视化球面的方式来说，

cues.en: This corresponds to slicing the sphere along the plane where x is 0.5 and looking at the circle formed by all of the choices for y and z on that sphere. As you increase the value of x, the amount of real estate left over for y and z is smaller, and this more constrained piston dance is what it feels like for the circular slice to be smaller. Eventually, once x reaches the value 1, there's no real estate left over, so you reach this singularity point.
cues.zh: 这相当于沿着 x 为 0.5 的平面切开球面，观察球面上所有 y 和 z 可能取值构成的圆。当你增大 x 的值时，留给 y 和 z 的地皮就会变少，而这种受到更大限制的活塞运动，直观反映出的就是圆形切片在变小。最终，一旦 x 达到 1，就没有任何地皮剩下了，于是你就到达了这个奇点。

cues.en: where y and z are both forced to be zero. The feeling here is a bit like being a bug on the surface of the sphere. You are unable to see the whole sphere all at once. Instead, you're just sitting on a single point, and you have some sense for what local movements are allowed. In four dimensions and higher, we lose the crutch of the global view that a spatial visual offers. But the fundamental rules of this real estate exchange remain the same.
cues.zh: 在这里，y 和 z 都被迫变为 0。这种感觉有点像一只爬在球面上的小虫子。你无法一眼看尽整个球体。相反，你只是停留在单一点上，隐约感知到允许进行哪些局部的移动。在四维及更高维度中，我们失去了空间直观带来的全局视野这一依托。但这种“地皮置换”的基本规则依然保持不变。

cues.en: If you fix one slider in place and watch the other three trade off, this is basically what it means to take a slice of the 4D sphere to get a small 3D sphere. In much the same way that fixing one of the sliders for the three-dimensional case give us a circular slice when the remaining two were free to vary. Now, watching these sliders move about and thinking about the real estate exchange is pretty fun.
cues.zh: 如果你固定住一个滑块，观察另外三个如何此消彼长，这基本上就是把四维球体切出一片、得到一个三维球体的含义。就像在三维情形中，固定三个滑块之一，让剩下两个自由变化时，我们会得到一个圆形切片。现在，看着这些滑块来回移动，并思考这种“地盘”交换，还挺有意思的。

cues.en: but it runs the risk of being aimless unless we have an actual high-dimensional puzzle to sink our teeth into. So let's set aside the sliders for just a moment and bring in a very classic example of something that seems reasonable and even dull in two and three dimensions, but which is totally out of whack in higher dimensions. To start, take a 2x2 box centered at the origin. Its corners are on the vertices 1 1, 1 negative 1, negative 1 1, and negative 1 negative 1.
cues.zh: 但如果我们没有一个具体的高维谜题去深入钻研，这就很容易失去方向。所以我们先暂时把这些滑块放到一旁，来看一个非常经典的例子，它在二维和三维空间里显得合情合理甚至平平无奇，但在更高维度下却完全变了样。首先，我们取一个以原点为中心的 2x2 正方形。它的四个角位于顶点 (1, 1)、(1, -1)、(-1, 1) 和 (-1, -1)。

cues.en: Draw four circles, each with radius 1, centered at these four vertices. So each one is tangent to two of its neighbors. Now I want you to think of the circle centered at the origin, which is just large enough to be touching those corner circles, tangent to each one of them. What we want to do for this setup, and for its analogies in higher dimensions, is find the radius of that inner circle.
cues.zh: 画四个半径为 1 的圆，圆心分别位于这四个顶点。这样每个圆都与两个相邻的圆相切。现在请想象以原点为圆心的那个圆，它刚好大到能碰到这些角上的圆，并与每一个都相切。对这个设置，以及它在更高维中的类比情形，我们要做的是求出那个内圆的半径。

cues.en: Here in two dimensions, we can use the Pythagorean theorem to see that the distance from the origin to the corner of the box is the square root of 2, which is around 1.414. Then you can subtract off this portion here the radius of the corner circle, which by definition is 1, and that means the radius of the inner circle is square root of 2 minus 1, or about 0.414. No surprises here, that seems pretty reasonable. Now do something analogous in three dimensions.
cues.zh: 在二维空间中，利用勾股定理可知，原点到盒子顶角的距离是根号 2，大约是 1.414。然后减去角上圆的半径这一部分（按定义半径为 1），就意味着内圆的半径是根号 2 减 1，也就是约 0.414。这里没什么意外的，看起来挺合情合理。现在，我们在三维空间中做类似的推导。

cues.en: Draw a 2x2x2 cube whose corners have vertices 1 1 1, 1 1 negative 1, on and on and on. And then we're going to take 8 different spheres, each of which has a radius 1, and center them on these vertices, so that each one is tangent to 3 of its neighbors. Now again, think about the sphere centered at the origin, which is just large enough to be barely touching those 8 corner spheres.
cues.zh: 画一个 2x2x2 的立方体，它的顶点坐标分别为 (1, 1, 1)、(1, 1, -1) 等等。然后我们取 8 个不同的球体，每个球的半径都是 1，球心分别位于这些顶点上，这样每个球都与它的 3 个相邻球相切。现在，再次想象一个以原点为中心的球体，它的大小刚好能够触碰到这 8 个角落上的球体。

cues.en: As before, we can start by thinking about the distance from the origin to the corner of the box, say the corner at 1, 1, 1. By the way, I guess I still haven't yet explicitly said that the way distances work in higher dimensions is always to add up the squares of the components in each direction and take the square root. If you've never seen why this follows from the Pythagorean Theorem just in the two-dimensional case, it's actually a really fun puzzle to think about.
cues.zh: 和之前一样，我们可以先考虑从原点到立方体顶角的距离，比如 (1, 1, 1) 这个角。顺便提一句，我好像一直没明说，高维空间中计算距离的方法，始终是把各个方向分量的平方相加再开平方根。如果你还没想过这怎么由二维的勾股定理推导出来，那这其实是个特别有意思的小谜题。

cues.en: and I've left the relevant image up on the screen for any of you who want to pause and ponder on it. Anyway, in our case, the distance between the origin and the corner 1 1 1 is the square root of 1 squared plus 1 squared plus 1 squared, or square root of 3, which is about 1.73. So the radius of that inner sphere is going to be this quantity minus the radius of a corner sphere, which by definition is 1. And again,
cues.zh: 屏幕上留着对应的图，想暂停思考的可以看一下。总之在我们的例子中，原点到角落 (1, 1, 1) 的距离是根号下 1 平方加 1 平方加 1 平方，也就是根号 3，大约是 1.73。所以内层球体的半径就是这个数值减去角球的半径，按定义角球半径是 1。而且，

cues.en: 0.73 seems like a reasonable radius for that inner sphere. But what happens to that inner radius as you increase dimensions? Obviously the reason I bring this up is that something surprising will happen, and some of you might see where this is going. But I actually don't want it to feel like a surprise. As fun as it is to wow people with counterintuitive facts in math, the goal here is genuine understanding, not shock.
cues.zh: 内球半径是 0.73 看起来挺合情合理的。但如果维度增加，这个内球半径会变成什么样？显然我提到这一点，是因为接下来会有出人意料的事情发生，可能有些人已经猜到了。但我其实不希望它显得太意外。用反直觉的数学事实让人惊叹固然有趣，但这里的目标是真正理解，而不是为了震惊。

cues.en: For higher dimensions, we'll be using sliders to get a gut feel for what's going on. But since it's kind of a different way of viewing things, it helps to get a running start by looking back at how to analyze the two- and three-dimensional cases in the context of sliders. First things first, how do you think about a circle centered at a corner, like one negative one? Previously, for a circle centered at the origin, the amount of real estate belonging to both x and y was dependent on their distance from the number zero.
cues.zh: 对于更高维度，我们会用滑块来建立直观感受。但由于这是一种略有不同的观察方式，先回过头看看怎么用滑块的角度分析二维和三维情况，会很有帮助。首先，你怎么理解一个以某个角为中心（比如 (1, -1)）的圆？之前对于以原点为中心的圆，x 和 y 各自占有的空间，取决于它们到数字 0 的距离。

cues.en: And it's the same basic idea here as you move around the center, it's just that the real estate might be dependent on the distance between each coordinate and some other number. So for this circle, centered at 1, negative 1, the amount of real estate belonging to X is the square of its distance from 1. Likewise, the real estate belonging to Y is the square of its distance from negative 1. Other than that, the looking feel with this piston dance trade-off is completely the same.
cues.zh: 这里的基本思想也是一样的，就算你移动圆心，也只是每个坐标占有的空间取决于它到另一个数字的距离而已。所以对于这个以 (1, -1) 为中心的圆，X 占有的空间就是它到 1 的距离的平方。同理，Y 占有的空间就是它到 -1 的距离的平方。除此之外，这种像活塞运动般的权衡感受是完全一样的。

cues.en: For simplicity, we'll only focus on one of these circles, the one centered at 1, 1. Now ask yourself, what does it mean to find a circle centered at the origin, large enough to be tangent to this guy, when we're thinking just in terms of sliders? Well, notice how this point of tangency happens when the x and y coordinates are both the same. Or phrase differently, at the point of this corner circle, closest to the origin, the real estate is shared evenly between x and y.
cues.zh: 为了简便起见，我们只关注其中一个圆，也就是以 (1, 1) 为中心的那个。现在问问自己，单从滑块的角度来看，找到一个以原点为中心、大到刚好与它相切的圆，究竟意味着什么？大家注意看，这个切点刚好发生在 x 和 y 坐标完全相等的时候。或者换种说法，在这个角圆上距离原点最近的点，x 和 y 平分了占有的空间。

cues.en: This will be important for later, so let's really dig in and think about why it's true. Imagine perturbing that point slightly, maybe moving x a little closer to 0, which means y would have to move a little away from 0. The change in x would have to be a little smaller than the change in y, since the real estate it gains by moving farther away from 1 is more expensive than the real estate that y loses by getting closer to 1. But from the perspective of the origin point, 0, 0, that trade-off is reversed.
cues.zh: 这一点对后面至关重要，所以我们深入探究一下为什么会这样。想象对那个点做微小的扰动，比如让 x 稍微靠近 0 一点，这就意味着 y 必须远离 0 一点。x 的变化量必须比 y 的变化量稍微小一点，因为 x 远离 1 所增加的占用代价，要高于 y 靠近 1 所减少的占用。但从原点 (0, 0) 的角度来看，这种权衡关系恰好反了过来。

cues.en: The resulting change to x-squared is smaller than the resulting change to y-squared since when real estate is measured with respect to 0-0 that move of y towards 1 is the more expensive one. What this means is that any slight perturbation away from this point where real estate is shared evenly results in an increasing distance from the origin. The reason we care is that this point is tangent to the inner circle
cues.zh: x 平方带来的变化小于 y 平方带来的变化，因为以 (0,0) 为基准衡量“占地”时，y 向 1 的移动代价更大。这意味着，从这个“占地”均分的点稍微扰动，都会导致到原点的距离增大。我们关心它，是因为这个点与内圆相切。

cues.en: So we can also think about it as being a point of the inner circle. And this will be very useful for higher dimensions. It gives us a reference point to understanding the radius of that inner circle. Specifically, you can ask how much real estate is shared between x and y at this point when real estate measurements are done with respect to the origin, 0,0. For example, down here in two dimensions, both x and y dip below 0.5 in this configuration.
cues.zh: 所以我们也可以把它看作内圆上的一个点。这对更高维度非常有用。它给了我们一个参考点，用来理解那个内圆的半径。具体来说，在以此原点 (0,0) 为基准衡量“占地”时，你可以问在这个点上 x 和 y 共享了多少“占地”。例如，在二维的这里，这个配置下 x 和 y 都低于 0.5。

cues.en: So the total value x squared plus y squared is going to be less than 0.5 squared plus 0.5 squared. Comparing to this halfway point is really going to come in handy for wrapping our mind around what happens in higher dimensions. Taking things one step at a time, let's bump it up to three dimensions. Consider the corner sphere with radius 1 centered at 1, 1, 1. The point on that sphere that's closest to the origin
cues.zh: 所以 x 平方加 y 平方的总值会小于 0.5 平方加 0.5 平方。和这个半程点作比较，会非常有助于我们理解更高维中发生的事。一步一步来，我们升到三维。考虑半径为 1、中心在 (1,1,1) 的角球。那个球面上离原点最近的点

cues.en: corresponds to the configuration of sliders where x, y, and z are all reaching down towards zero and equal to each other. Again, they all have to go a little beyond that halfway point, because the position 0.5 only accounts for 0.5 squared, or 0.25 units of real estate. So with all three coordinates getting a third of a unit of real estate, they need to be farther out. And again,
cues.zh: 对应于滑块的一种配置：x、y、z 都朝零靠近，并且彼此相等。再说一次，它们都必须稍微越过那个半程点，因为位置 0.5 只对应 0.5 平方，也就是 0.25 单位的“占地”。所以当三个坐标各分到三分之一个单位的“占地”时，它们需要更靠外。并且，再一次，

cues.en: Since this is a point where the corner sphere is tangent to the inner sphere, it's also a point of the inner sphere. So, with reference to the origin, 0, 0, 0, think about the amount of real estate shared between x, y, and z in this position, corresponding to the tangent point. It's definitely less than 0.75, since all three of these are smaller than 0.5, so each one has less than 0.25 units of real estate.
cues.zh: 由于这是角球与内球相切的点，它也是内球上的一个点。那么，以原点 (0,0,0) 为基准，想想在这个切点位置上 x、y、z 共享的“占地”总量。它肯定小于 0.75，因为这三个都小于 0.5，所以每个都拥有少于 0.25 单位的“占地”。

cues.en: And again, we sit back and feel comfortable with this result, right? The inner sphere is smaller than the corner spheres. But things get interesting when we move up into four dimensions. Our 2x2x2x2 box is going to have 16 vertices at 1111, 111-1, and so on, with all possible binary combinations of 1 and negative 1. What this means is that there are 16 unit spheres centered at these corners.
cues.zh: 同样，我们可以安心接受这个结果，对吧？内球比角球小。但当我们升到四维时，事情就变得有趣了。我们的 2x2x2x2 盒子里会有 16 个顶点，位于 1111、111-1 等等，涵盖 1 和 -1 的所有二进制组合。这意味着有 16 个单位球以这些角点为中心。

cues.en: each one tangent to four of its neighbors. As before, we'll just be focusing on one of them, the one centered at 1, 1, 1, 1. The point of this sphere closest to the origin corresponds to the configuration of sliders where all four coordinates reach exactly halfway between 1 and 0. And that's because when one of the coordinates is 0.5 units away from 1, it has 0.25 units of real estate with respect to the point 1.
cues.zh: 每个球都与它的四个邻居相切。和之前一样，我们只关注其中一个，也就是以 (1,1,1,1) 为中心的那个。这个球上离原点最近的点，对应于滑块的一种配置：四个坐标都恰好到达 1 和 0 之间的中点。这是因为，当其中一个坐标距离 1 为 0.5 个单位时，相对于点 1，它拥有 0.25 单位的“占地”。

cues.en: We do the same trick as before, thinking of this now as a point of the inner sphere and measuring things with respect to the origin, but you can already see what's cool about four dimensions. As you switch to thinking of real estate with respect to 0000, it's still the case that each of these four coordinates has 0.25 units of real estate, making for a total of one shared between the four coordinates. In other words, that inner sphere is precisely the same size as the corner spheres.
cues.zh: 我们故技重施，现在把它看作内球上的一个点，并以原点为基准来度量，但你已经能看出四维空间的妙处了。当你转而以 0000 为基准来考虑配额时，这四个坐标依然各占 0.25 个单位的配额，四个坐标平分刚好总共为 1。换句话说，那个内球和角落里的球大小完全相同。

cues.en: This matches with what you see numerically, by the way, where you can compute the distance between the origin and the corner, 1, 1, 1, 1, is the square root of 4, and then when you subtract off the radius of one of the corner spheres, what you get is 1. But there's something much more satisfying about seeing it, rather than just computing it. In particular, here's a cool aspect of the fact that that inner sphere has radius 1. Move things around so that all of the real estate goes to the coordinate x, and you'll end up at the point
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，这也符合数值计算的结果，你可以算出原点与角落点 1, 1, 1, 1 之间的距离是 4 的平方根，然后再减去角落球的半径，得到的结果就是 1。但比起单纯的计算，亲眼看到这种现象要令人满意得多。特别是，关于这个半径为 1 的内球，还有一个很酷的现象。调整各项数值，把所有的配额都分配给坐标 x，你最终会落在点

cues.en: 1, 0, 0, 0. This point is actually touching the 2x2x2x2 box. And when you're stuck thinking in the two or three-dimensional cases, this fact that the inner sphere has radius 1, the same size as the corner spheres, and that it touches the box, well, it just seems too big. But it's important to realize this is fundamentally a four-dimensional phenomenon, and you just can't cram it down into smaller dimensions. But things get weirder.
cues.zh: 1, 0, 0, 0。这个点实际上正接触着 2x2x2x2 的超立方体外框。如果你还停留在二维或三维的思维模式中，面对内球半径为 1、与角落球等大、甚至接触到外框的事实，难免会觉得它太大了。但重要的是要意识到，这本质上是四维空间的特有现象，你根本无法把它硬塞进更低的维度里。不过，事情还会变得更诡异。

cues.en: Let's knock it up to five dimensions. In this case, we have quite a few corner spheres, 32 in total. But again, for simplicity, we'll only be thinking about the one centered at 11111. Think about the point of this sphere closest to the origin, where all five coordinates are equally splitting the one unit of shared real estate. This time, each coordinate is a little higher than 0.5. If they reach down to 0.5,
cues.zh: 我们把它提升到五维。在这种情况下，角落球相当多，总共有 32 个。但同样为了简便起见，我们只考虑以 11111 为中心的那一个。考虑这个球上离原点最近的点，此时五个坐标均分总共为 1 个单位的配额。这一次，每个坐标的值都略高于 0.5。如果它们刚好低至 0.5，

cues.en: Each one would have 0.25 units of real estate, giving a total of 1.25, which is too much. But the tables are turned when you view this as a point on the inner sphere. Because with respect to the origin, this configuration has much more than one unit of real estate. Not only is every coordinate more than 0.5 units away from zero, but the larger number of dimensions means that there's more total real estate when you add it all up.
cues.zh: 那么每个坐标都会占用 0.25 个单位的配额，总计就是 1.25，这显然超标了。但当你把它看作内球上的一个点时，情况就完全逆转了。因为以原点为基准，这种配置所拥有的配额远不止 1 个单位。不仅每个坐标与零点的距离都大于 0.5 个单位，而且维度数量的增加意味着，把它们全部加起来后的总配额会更多。

cues.en: Specifically, you can compute that the radius of that inner sphere is about 1.24. The intuitive feel for what that means is that the sliders can roam over more territory than what just a single unit of real estate would allow. One fun way to see what this means is to adjust everything so that all of the real estate goes to just one coordinate. Because this coordinate can reach beyond one, what you are seeing is that this five-dimensional inner sphere
cues.zh: 具体来说，你可以算出那个内球的半径大约是 1.24。这种直观感受意味着，滑块可以活动的空间比单单 1 个单位配额所允许的要大得多。要直观理解这代表着什么，一个有趣的办法就是调整所有数值，把所有的配额全部分给单一坐标。由于这个坐标的值可以超过 1，你所看到的就是这个五维内球

cues.en: actually pokes outside the box. But to really get a feel for how strange things become, as a last example I want to jump up into 10 dimensions. Remember, all this means is that points have 10 coordinates. For a sphere with radius 1, a single unit of real estate must be shared among all 10 of those coordinates. As always, the point of this corner sphere closest to the origin is the one where all 10 coordinates split the real estate evenly.
cues.zh: 实际上已经戳出了外框。但为了真正感受事情会变得多么不可思议，作为最后一个例子，我想直接跳到十维空间。记住，这仅仅意味着点拥有 10 个坐标而已。对于一个半径为 1 的球，1 个单位的配额必须由这全部 10 个坐标共同分摊。和之前一样，这个角落球上离原点最近的点，就是所有 10 个坐标均分配额的点。

cues.en: And here you can really see just how far away this feels from the origin. Or phrased differently, that inner sphere is allowed to have a very large amount of real estate. In fact, you can compute that the radius of the inner sphere is about 2.16. And viewed from this perspective, where you have 10 full dimensions to share that real estate, doesn't it actually feel somewhat reasonable that the inner sphere
cues.zh: 在这里你能真切感受到，它离原点有多远。换个说法，那个内球可以占据非常大的空间。事实上，可以算出内球半径约为 2.16。从这个角度看，你有整整 10 个维度来分配这些空间，那么内球的

cues.en: should have a radius more than twice as big as all those corner spheres. To get a sense for just how big this inner sphere is, look back in two dimensions and imagine a 4x4 box bounding all four circles from the outside. Or go to three dimensions and imagine a 4x4x4 box bounding all of those corner spheres from the outside. Way up here in 10 dimensions, that quote-unquote inner sphere
cues.zh: 半径超过所有那些角球的两倍，是不是其实感觉挺合理？要感受这个内球到底有多大，回到二维，想象一个从外面包住四个圆的 4x4 方框。或者到三维，想象一个从外面包住所有那些角球的 4x4x4 方框。在 10 维这里，那个所谓的“内球”

cues.en: is actually large enough to poke outside of that outer bounding box, since it has a diameter bigger than 4. I know that seems crazy, but you have to realize that the face of the box is always two units away from the origin, no matter how high the dimension is. And fundamentally, it's because it only involves moving along a single axis. But the point 111111111 which determines the inner sphere's radius
cues.zh: 其实大到能戳出那个外包框，因为它的直径大于 4。我知道这听起来很疯狂，但你要意识到，无论维度多高，方框的面到原点始终是两个单位。根本上说，这是因为只涉及沿单一坐标轴移动。但决定内球半径的点 111111111

cues.en: is actually really far away from the center all the way up here in 10 dimensions. And it's because all 10 of those dimensions add a full unit of real estate for that point. And of course, as you keep upping the dimensions, that inner sphere just keeps growing without bound. Not only is it poking outside of these boxes, but the proportion of the inner sphere lying inside the box decreases exponentially towards zero as the dimension keeps increasing.
cues.zh: 在 10 维这里其实离中心非常远。因为那 10 个维度都分别为这个点增加了一整单位的空间。当然，随着维度不断提高，这个内球会一直无界增长。它不仅戳出这些方框，而且内球位于方框内的比例会随着维度增加而指数级趋近于零。

cues.en: So taking a step back, one of the things I like about using this slider method for teaching is that when I shared it with a few friends, the way they started to talk about higher dimensions became a little less metaphysical and started to sound more like how you would hear a mathematician talk about the topic. Rather than skeptically asking whether or not ten-dimensional space is a real thing, recognizing that it's exactly as real as numbers are, people would actually probe at what other properties high dimensional spheres have.
cues.zh: 退一步说，我喜欢用这种滑块方法教学的一点是，当我和几个朋友分享它时，他们谈论高维的方式变得没那么玄乎了，开始更像你听到数学家讨论这个话题。人们不再怀疑十维空间是不是真实存在，而是认识到它和数字一样真实，并会去探究高维球体还有哪些其他性质。

cues.en: and what other shapes feel like in terms of sliders. This box situation is just one in a number of things that feel very crazy about higher dimensional spheres, and it's really fun to think about these others in the context of sliders and real estate. It's obviously limited. I mean, you're a bug on the surface of these objects, only getting a feel for one point at a time and for the rules of movement. Also, geometry can be quite nice when it's coordinate free, and this is the opposite of that.
cues.zh: 以及其他形状用滑块来感受是什么样。这个方框情形只是高维球体众多让人感觉非常疯狂的事情之一，在滑块和空间的语境下思考其他这些情形真的很有趣。它显然有局限。我的意思是，你是这些物体表面的一只虫子，一次只能感受一个点和移动规则。另外，几何在无坐标时可能相当美妙，而这恰恰相反。

cues.en: But it does give a foothold into thinking about high dimensional shapes a little more concretely. Now you could say that viewing things with sliders is no different from thinking about things purely analytically. I mean, it's honestly little more than representing each coordinate literally. It's kind of the most obvious thing you might do. But this small move makes it much more possible to play with the thought of a high dimensional point. And even little things, like thinking about the squares of coordinates as real estate,
cues.zh: 但这确实为我们更具体地思考高维形状提供了一个立足点。你可能会说，用滑块观察事物和纯粹的解析思考没什么两样。我的意思是，这其实不过就是把每个坐标字面化地表示出来而已。这几乎是你最顺理成章能想到的做法。但正是这一小步，让我们更有可能把玩“高维点”这一概念。甚至连一些小技巧，比如把坐标的平方看作面积地块，

cues.en: can shed light on some seemingly strange aspects of high dimensions, like just how far away the corner of a box is from its center. If anything, the fact that it's such a direct representation of a purely analytic description is exactly what makes it such a faithful reflection of what genuinely doing math in higher dimensions entails. We're still flying in the clouds, trusting the instruments of analytic reasoning, but this is a redesign of those instruments.
cues.zh: 也能帮我们搞懂高维空间中一些看似怪异的特性，比如一个盒子的角落离它的中心到底有多远。退一步说，正因为它如此直接地体现了纯分析式的描述，才使它如此忠实地反映了在高维空间中真正做数学的本质。我们依然是在云端飞行，依赖着解析推理的仪表，但这相当于重新设计了这些仪表。

cues.en: One which better takes advantage of the fact that such a large portion of our brains goes towards image processing. I mean, just because you can't visualize something doesn't mean you can't still think about it visually.
cues.zh: 这种设计更好地利用了我们大脑有很大一部分专门用于图像处理这一优势。我的意思是，你无法直接想象出某个事物，并不意味着你不能以视觉化的方式去思考它。
